lines_only_in_build: The General Services Administration says DCAT-US version 3.0 was built together by the Federal Chief Data Officers Council, the Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM), and the Data.gov team. Their joint effort is the FAIRness Project (FAIR: findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable).

The Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) report A Framework for Data Quality says documentation should include methods used in processing, imputations, weighting, editing, integration methods, and data dictionaries. Data on the Web Best Practices (2017) intends that people learn a dataset's origin and history and that computer programs process this provenance automatically, and tests for that. The Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) Version 3 says quality dimensions are characteristics that matter to users, sets no required list, and leaves implementers to choose their own. StatDCAT-AP, a statistical catalog profile, and the Data Cube vocabulary name each breakdown as its own field in the record, not in a written description of variables.
The FAIRness Project's two-year sequencing plan, a plan for transition, went to the Office of Management and Budget and was not published; a 2024 public request remains unanswered.
lines_only_in_v2: The General Services Administration says DCAT-US version 3.0 was built together by the Federal Chief Data Officers Council, FCSM, and the Data.gov team. Their joint effort is the FAIRness Project (FAIR: findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable).

FCSM's A Framework for Data Quality says documentation should include methods used in processing, imputations, weighting, editing, integration methods, and data dictionaries. Data on the Web Best Practices (2017) intends that people learn a dataset's origin and history and that computer programs process this provenance automatically. DCAT Version 3 says quality dimensions are characteristics that matter to users, sets no required list, and leaves implementers to choose their own. StatDCAT-AP and the W3C Data Cube vocabulary name each breakdown, such as place or time, as its own field in the record.
The FAIRness Project's two-year sequencing plan went to OMB and was not published; a 2024 public request remains unanswered.
